proposal.root_cause: Projection convention mismatch: entity questions answered with narrow/DISTINCT columns instead of gold's full joined rows, and 1:N join fan-out left undeduplicated
proposal.what: Rewrite system_prompt.md's output-shape rules into an explicit decision procedure: when the question asks 'which/what <entities>' without naming attributes, select all columns of the driving table (or * across joined tables); use DISTINCT only when duplicates would be wrong (dedup join fan-out); keep named-attribute projections narrow. Prompt-only change, no extra policy calls.

proposal.raw:
Diagnosis: three of the four failures (sp0536, sp0600, sp0755) are *projection/dedup* mistakes on drafts that execute fine with non-empty results — the model emits a narrow `SELECT DISTINCT name` where Spider gold returns full joined rows (`T1.*` / `*`), or keeps join fan-out duplicates. The existing prompt rule ("return the full rows") is too weak/conditional for this policy, and the repair loop never fires because the result is non-empty. Prior attempts to fix this via extra shape-diagnostic calls were rejected on cost/degenerate triggers, so this edit stays prompt-only (zero added tokens/calls) and makes the default projection explicit and unconditional for entity questions.
